title: Crossing the Gender Binary: Modelling Gendered Reference in Science Fiction and General Fiction
measurement_description: The study evaluated the linguistic distribution and masked language modeling predictions for gendered terms ('man', 'woman', 'person') in literature. In terms of religion, it measured the frequency and context in which masking the word 'woman' resulted in top lexical substitute predictions that named specific religious categories. This was used to demonstrate how the predictive semantic neighborhood of female reference intersects with other marked social identities.
findings: The paper found that when occurrences of the word 'woman' or 'women' were masked, the model occasionally predicted terms associated with marked social, racial, and religious groups—specifically including 'Jews', 'Muslims', and 'Christians'—among its top candidate sets. In contrast, these religious and identity-based terms were largely absent from the candidate sets when 'man' or 'men' were masked. The findings suggest that in the linguistic training data, 'woman' shares a structural predictive neighborhood with other marginalized or distinctly classified social groups, while 'man' functions more as an unmarked implicit human standard.
